source_admission: Its lake relations, the land's loss and people's losses are the phosphorus study's, whose sources and how far each was read are in resources/sea_phosphorus_sources.json. The dust rests on two project notes and the nitrogen on one outside source, checked on 22 November 2026 by a search summary only. Values the README marks as recalled were not looked up.

sources.citation: Dust, salt and fog aerosol over the Open Moon's dry plains: literature values (the aerosol study's note, 5 October 2026)
sources.use: The vertical dust flux as F = alpha Q with Earth's alpha of 1e-5 to 1e-4 per metre (Kok et al. 2012; González-Flórez et al. 2023), and the note's central choice that alpha follows gravity at the Moon, 0.165 of Earth's (Lu & Shao 1999; Shao 2004), with alpha unscaled as its high scheme (Marticorena & Bergametti 1995)

sources.citation: Lewis WM, Melack JM, McDowell WH, McClain M, Richey JE 1999, Nitrogen yields from undisturbed watersheds in the Americas, Biogeochemistry 46, 149-162
sources.use: Total nitrogen leaving undisturbed tropical watersheds, 5.1 kg per hectare a year on average, 70% of it dissolved, rising with runoff at about two thirds of its rate: the high end of the land's nitrogen loss, with a low end of a fifth of it for the Open Moon's drier land chosen here
